claims.feature: Forgotten Realms terms in the general guide
claims.claim: The general guide carries a short Realms list: Goodman/Goodwoman capped, 'goodsir' lowercased, 'godsforsaken' as the Realms form of godforsaken, and 'the Realms' only after 'the Forgotten Realms'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')
claims.quote: goodsir (a form of address, not capped)

claims.claim: 'Godsforsaken' is the established Realms form but is not required in other polytheistic settings, since 'godforsaken' has no necessary monotheistic sense.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: 'Fellowship' is avoided for a party because of its Tolkien association and because D&D parties are often fractious or mercenary; 'party', 'group', 'band', or 'company' are preferred.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: Standard abbreviations are fixed (PH, DMG, MM, gp, d100, AC, DC, DM, XP, HD, hp, NPC).
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019')

claims.claim: The superseded 2013 guide banned singular they outside informal contexts like dialogue.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)
claims.quote: Don’t use “they” or “their” as singular pronouns

claims.claim: The 2013 guide framed gender neutrality as assuming a readership of both men and women, a framing dropped in 2019 for 'we don't assume a gender identity'.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)
claims.quote: readership includes both men and women

claims.claim: Sections absent from v1.04a and present in v1.08a include Gender-Specific Suffixes, Headings, Sidebars, Bulleted Lists, Appendix References, and Adventuring Parties (verified by heading presence in both texts).
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.04a (2013)

claims.feature: existence of a post-2019 house style guide
claims.claim: A Word version of the house style guide, authored by Kim Mohan and last modified by Judy Bauer on 2021-07-06 at Wizards of the Coast, ships inside the Dungeoncraft Pack (2023-12-04) and postdates the public v1.08a PDF.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 docx cites merriam-webster.com rather than the printed 11th edition Collegiate.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: The 2021 docx reverses the 2019 rule: 'man' and 'woman' may now describe the gender of any people, so 'dwarf man' and 'gnome woman' are fine.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: we can write “dwarf man” or “gnome woman.”

claims.claim: The 2021 docx allows they/their/them/themself for a person of unknown gender without the 2019 'don't abuse this liberty' caveat, requiring only a clear antecedent.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: you must ensure that the pronoun’s antecedent is clear

claims.claim: In running text a person's preferred pronoun (he, she, or they) is used; in rules text 'it' is used.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.claim: Descriptive text uses they/them for Humanoids and other sapient creatures of unknown gender (including vampires), and 'it' for animals, cosmic horrors, and extraplanar creatures.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
claims.quote: A beholder never keeps its promises.

claims.claim: Where 'they' would be ambiguous the sentence is reworded to avoid pronouns, e.g. by switching to the plural.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

claims.feature: 'it' for dehumanizing effect is an exception
claims.claim: Using 'it' for a sapient monster to emphasize inhumanity is allowed only as a rare deliberate effect.
claims.source: DnD House Style Guide.docx (Wizards of the Coast; created Kim Mohan 2016-03-07, last modified Judy Bauer 2021-07-06) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04

verdicts.trueWording: goodsir (a form of address, not capped)
verdicts.note: Raw PDF text extracted (pdfminer + pypdf). p.9 'Forgotten Realms Terms' list carries verbatim 'Goodman/Goodwoman (a title or form of address, usu. capped)', 'godsforsaken (established in the Realms...)', 'goodsir (a form of address, not capped)'; the list continues on p.10 with 'the Realms (should be preceded by “the Forgotten Realms”)'. All four limbs supported. Only hedge: source says 'usu. capped', claim says 'capped'.

verdicts.trueWording: godsforsaken (established in the Realms, but not necessary in other polytheistic settings; “godforsaken” has no necessary connection to monotheism)
verdicts.note: Quote fragment appears word for word on p.9 of the v1.08a PDF; every limb of the claim (established Realms form, not necessary elsewhere, godforsaken has no necessary monotheistic connection) is the source's own wording.

p.9 'Adventuring Parties' sidebar, verbatim: 'The word “fellowship” has strong connections with The Lord of the Rings and doesn’t represent the typical D&D adventuring party well... D&D adventuring companies are often fractious or more mercenary than the word “fellowship” implies. In most in-world contexts and all other contexts, use “group,” “band,” “company,” or, especially, “party.”' All three limbs (Tolkien association, fractious/mercenary, four preferred words) supported.

pypdf page-10 reconstruction gives the table row verbatim: 'HD Hit Die/Dice \n hp hit points \n NPC nonplayer character'. Every abbreviation named in the claim is present in the p.10 Abbreviations tables: PH, DMG, MM (Brand/Product), gp (Coin), d100 (Die), AC, DC, DM, XP, HD, hp, NPC (Other Term).

verdicts.trueWording: Don’t use “they” or “their” as singular pronouns, except in an informal context like dialogue.
verdicts.note: v1.04a PDF confirmed (footer 'Version 1.04a ©2013 Wizards of the Coast'); quote is verbatim on p.2 under 'Achieving Gender Neutrality'. Both limbs (ban; informal-context/dialogue exception) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: We also assume that our readership includes both men and women.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim on p.2 of v1.04a. The second limb checks out against v1.08a: the 2019 guide has zero occurrences of 'readership' and its Gender section instead reads 'We don’t assume that our readers are of a particular gender identity.' Note the claim's inline rendering 'we don’t assume a gender identity' is a compression, not the 2019 wording.

verdicts.trueWording: Five of the six are new headings; 'Bulleted Lists' renames v1.04a's 'Vertical Lists'.
verdicts.note: Both raw texts extracted and grepped. Heading-string counts: Gender-Specific Suffixes 0/2, Headings 0/4, Sidebars 0/3, Bulleted Lists 0/1, Appendix References 0/1, Adventuring Parties 0/1 (2013/2019). v1.04a's full heading roster was enumerated and contains none of the six strings; its only 'sidebar'/'heading' mentions are passing references inside 'Subsection/Table References' and 'Inline Subheads', and it has zero occurrences of 'appendix', 'appendices', 'suffix' or 'fellowship'. So five limbs are genuinely new sections; the sixth is a rename, which the claim's word 'Sections' over-states even though its parenthetical scopes verification to heading presence. No quote field, so VERBATIM is inapplicable in any case.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: “Bulleted Lists” as a section absent from v1.04a — v1.04a has “Vertical Lists” covering the same ground (complete-sentence lead-in + colon, capitalized items, closing punctuation only for complete sentences); it is a rename, not a new section.

verdicts.trueWording: creator Kim Mohan; lastModifiedBy 'Bauer, Judy'; modified 2021-07-06; Company Wizards of the Coast.
verdicts.note: Zip fetched (HTTP 200, 1,624,152 bytes) and expanded; 'Dungeoncraft Pack/DnD House Style Guide.docx' present, zip entry dated 12-04-2023 matching the pack URL. docProps/core.xml verbatim: <dc:creator>Kim Mohan</dc:creator>, <cp:lastModifiedBy>Bauer, Judy</cp:lastModifiedBy>, <dcterms:created>2016-03-07T20:43:00Z</dcterms:created>, <dcterms:modified>2021-07-06T18:09:00Z</dcterms:modified>; docProps/app.xml <Company>Wizards of the Coast</Company>. 2021-07-06 postdates the v1.08a PDF (©2018, 'updated January 2019'). Empty quote field, so graded on substance.

docx body line 5, in the two-primary-resources list: 'The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition / merriam-webster.com'. The contrast limb holds: the docx has zero occurrences of 'Collegiate', while v1.08a p.1 reads 'Merriam-Webster’s Collegiate Dictionary, 11th edition'.

verdicts.trueWording: we can write “dwarf man” or “gnome woman.”
verdicts.note: docx 'Gender and Fantasy Races': '“Man,” “woman,” and their plurals are fine for describing the gender of people. For example, we can write “dwarf man” or “gnome woman.”' The reversal limb is confirmed against v1.08a p.2, which reads 'reserved for describing humans only. For example, we write “male dwarf,” not “dwarf man” or “man dwarf.”' — the exact phrase the docx now permits.

verdicts.trueWording: you must ensure that the pronoun’s antecedent is clear
verdicts.note: docx: 'We allow the use of “they,” “their,” “them,” and “themself” when referring to a person whose gender is unknown. But you must ensure that the pronoun’s antecedent is clear if more than one person appears in the context.' All four pronouns present; docx has zero occurrences of 'abuse this liberty', which v1.08a carries ('but don’t abuse this liberty. Rely on this device only when you have no other reasonable or pleasing alternative').

docx 'Pronoun Preference' — 'Short Version: In running text, use a person’s preferred pronoun: he, she, or they. Whatever pronoun you use, ensure that its antecedent is clear. In rules text, use “it.”' Both limbs verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: A beholder never keeps its promises.
verdicts.note: docx 'Pronouns for Generic Creatures', descriptive-text bullets: 'Use they/them pronouns for Humanoids and other sapient creatures that have gender identity, but when we don’t know their gender identity...'; 'Use “it” otherwise (animals, cosmic horrors, extraplanar creatures, etc.)'; and under '“They/them” in Descriptive Text' — 'But Also… vampires (Undead that retain their identity)'. The quote is the closing example under '“It” in Descriptive Text'. Every limb, vampires included, supported.

verdicts.trueWording: If using they/them pronouns would be ambiguous, reword to avoid using pronouns.
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the docx. The plural limb is supported twice: the 'Avoid Ambiguity' example offers 'OR “Merfolk attack elves on sight.”', and 'Sidestep Edge Cases' gives 'Blorvents are friendly, but they rust easily. (switching to plural to avoid choosing between “they” and “it”)'. Worth noting the first-listed cure is repeating the noun ('the merfolk immediately attacks'), with the plural as the alternative.

docx 'Limited Exceptions': 'On occasion, we might make exceptions to the guidelines above to achieve a specific effect. For example, characters might use gendered pronouns to talk about an animated doll, or we might use “it” to emphasize the inhumanity of a horrible monster (example). Such exceptions should be rare.' The word 'sapient' is not literally used but is entailed — an 'it' is an exception only for a creature the guidelines above would otherwise give they/them.
